artists.biography:
Creedence Clearwater Revival (often abbreviated CCR) was an American rock band that gained popularity in the late 1960s and early 1970s with a number of successful singles drawn from various albums.

The group consisted of lead vocalist, lead guitarist, and primary lyricist John Fogerty, his brother and rhythm guitarist Tom Fogerty, bassist Stu Cook, and drummer Doug Clifford. Their musical style encompassed rock and roll and swamp rock genres. Despite their San Francisco Bay Area origins, they are sometimes also cited as southern rock stylists.

CCR's music is still a staple of American and worldwide radio airplay and often figures in various media. The band has sold 26 million albums in the United States alone. CCR was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1993

apple_music.editorial_notes: Creedence Clearwater Revival’s Pendulum—amazingly, their sixth album in three years—is a heavier affair, with some of its songs (“Pagan Baby”) seemingly influenced by garage-style bands like The Stooges. Still, many aspects of these tracks maintain CCR’s trademark bluesy levity, like the funky keyboards of “Chameleon” and, of course, the lyrical grandness of “Have You Ever Seen the Rain?”, which is one of John Fogerty’s most enduring songs. Pendulum, with its crisp immediacy and soulful grooves, remains a gem.

lastfm.wiki_content: Pendulum is the sixth album by American band Creedence Clearwater Revival, released in 1970 (see 1970 in music). It was also the final Creedence album with rhythm guitarist Tom Fogerty, who left the group in February 1971 to start a solo career. The group continued as a trio. The most sonically adventurous of Creedence albums, the "surprisingly durable" (Robert Christgau) Pendulum is noted for its widespread use of horns and keyboards, in contrast to the group's previous albums, which were dominated by guitar. Among several lesser-known Fogerty songs ("Pagan Baby," "Sailor's Lament," "It's Just a Thought") were two top-ten hits, "Hey Tonight" and "Have You Ever Seen the Rain?". Both songs reached number eight in 1971. It also contains their only avant-garde venture, "Rude Awakening #2". The 1987 CD reissue of the album notes that the record was more experimental for the time period, and that it was highly regarded among popular-music fans, noting it's "universally acknowledged as among the greatest in the annals of rock." perplexity.description:
Pendulum is Creedence Clearwater Revival’s sixth studio album, released in 1970 on Fantasy Records. Arriving just months after Cosmo’s Factory, it captures the band at a peak of commercial momentum while showing a slightly broader, more deliberate approach than their earlier swamp-rock attack. The album includes some of CCR’s best-known later singles, including “Have You Ever Seen the Rain?” and “Hey Tonight,” and it is also notable as the last Creedence album to feature rhythm guitarist Tom Fogerty.

Musically, Pendulum keeps the band’s lean, rootsy rock foundation intact while adding a heavier, more polished sound, with John Fogerty writing all ten songs. The record was well received and became one of the group’s major commercial successes, reaching the upper tiers of album charts and earning platinum status. Its mix of hook-driven singles, bluesy drive, and tighter studio production makes it a key late-period Creedence release and an important marker of the band’s final classic-era run.
